A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same self-taught lookahead (STL) research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebShop and Game-of-24 experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements and model-scaling results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds HotpotQA evaluations in Table 3 and discount-factor experiments in Table 6.

M1.justification: The core rollout, lookahead-target construction and value-model fine-tuning procedure remain. The HotpotQA adaptation adds candidate-action handling using retrieved similar entries and supplies possible next actions to the value model, changing its inputs for this task (Appendix E.2–E.4).

E1.justification: v1 evaluates WebShop and Game-of-24. v2 adds training and evaluation on HotpotQA, extending coverage to multi-hop question answering requiring Wikipedia retrieval and reasoning across entries.

E2.justification: v2 adds R1-Searcher as an evaluated comparator in the new HotpotQA comparison. The WebShop comparator membership is unchanged between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1, and Game-of-24 retains its gpt-4o and algorithmic-oracle comparators.

E3.justification: HotpotQA introduces 500 training rollouts, 50- and 500-question evaluations, four-step trajectories, and correctness determined by exact matching or a gpt-4o evaluator. Cost evaluation now includes fine-tuning expenses. The reported Game-of-24 evaluation sets change from 48 to 50 tasks each; this establishes a reported sample-size revision without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a discount-factor sensitivity study spanning gamma values from 0.75 to 1.0 (Appendix H, Table 6). The existing rationale-component ablation is revised and loses its success-rate column. The WebShop second-iteration failure analysis and Game-of-24 iteration analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use paired bootstrap significance testing with one million bootstrap samples and the same significance thresholds. v2 extends this reporting practice to HotpotQA without introducing a different uncertainty-estimation procedure or new repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds HotpotQA results, including 61.8 match rate for STL versus 56.4 for the base llama value model on 500 questions, and adds discount-factor results. Ablation Score entries change from 70.4 to 70.0 for the base model and from 76.4 to 78.3 for STL without explaining the revisions. Reported savings change from 37× to 23× against LATS and from 10× to 5× against greedy gpt-4o under expanded cost accounting. The main WebShop comparison scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 corrects Equation 4 to condition the rationale on the selected best successor state. It also removes v1's malformed greedy-selection Equation 7, which assigned a maximum numerical value to an action. These are limited formal corrections; the central lookahead formulation and Algorithm 1 remain, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of reward-free value-model self-improvement matching gpt-4o remains. v2 removes the first-demonstration novelty claim, replaces the abstract's 20% performance improvement and 37× savings with comparable performance and order-of-magnitude savings, and extends claimed applicability to multi-hop QA. The stated WebShop average-reward improvement is corrected from greater than 17% to greater than 7%.

C2.justification: New Appendix C explicitly identifies dependence on supplied task specifications and limits the experimental evidence to models up to 8 billion parameters. v2 also explains training-cost amortization and narrows the smaller-model interpretation to approaching gpt-4o performance. The explanation of failed multi-step simulation on WebShop remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies gamma = 1, five MCTS rollout iterations, branching factors, and HotpotQA prompts and implementation details. Appendix G provides numerical inference prices and a 4.5-hour A40 fine-tuning estimate costing approximately $1.76. The shared LoRA settings and code URL remain, but v1's generated-training-corpus token totals are removed; these disclosures do not establish changes to retained experimental settings.

R1.justification: v2 refines positioning around reward access during learning versus inference and adds references on retrieval-based RL, world models, episodic RL and self-improving alignment, including Search-R1 and R1-Searcher. The existing fitted-value-iteration, LLM self-improvement and agent-training discussions largely remain; the first-demonstration positioning is withdrawn.

P1.justification: The introduction and experimental narrative undergo substantial rewriting, with method motivation moved into the introduction and reward-access categories used throughout. Appendices are reorganized, the impact statement moves to Broader Impacts, and separate limitations and cost sections are introduced.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, and figures and tables are extensively reorganized. v2 adds the information-access diagram and HotpotQA, pricing and sensitivity tables, redraws the efficiency display, and removes the ablation success-rate column, cost-versus-success-rate panel and scaling average-score panel.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence and transparency behind the paper's central claims. HotpotQA tests generalization in another applied domain, while explicit fine-tuning costs repair an omission in the efficiency comparison. Disclosing and testing gamma improves reproducibility, and the corrected reward-improvement claim better matches the unchanged WebShop scores. These gains outweigh the loss of some diagnostic result breakdowns, although the revised ablation endpoints and Game-of-24 sample counts remain unexplained.
